solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Long movie, Elizabeth R, upended formula (6)

indicatorNotes.upended: turned end over end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an epic is a long film
the first letters of Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher
reversal indicator: both pieces together are stood on their heads

annotation.surface: A critic sums up a long royal biopic that turned history on its head as a formulaic film.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole of EPIC + ER flips, not just one part. ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher on British postboxes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the set formula a cook follows.

entries.clue: You could take a break here, or in lounge (6)

annotation.definition: You could take a break here

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places OR inside the word for lounge

annotation.surface: A holiday tip: take your break here, or just stay in the lounge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a joining word between two options but is literal fodder, dropped into REST.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the holiday destination people go to for a break.

entries.clue: Sixties film about star sign pop art - revolutionary (9)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: something revolutionary revolves, turning ART round

blocks.note: pop and pa both mean father
taken as it stands, then turned to TRA

annotation.surface: A description of a Sixties film about astrology and pop art with a radical streak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop art' reads as one phrase but splits: pop is PA, and art is turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the 1963 Elizabeth Taylor epic is a film of the Sixties.

entries.clue: 'Pier cut performing job with car' - daughter's message from seaside? (7,8)

indicatorNotes.performing: the letters of 'pier cut' put on a show in a new order
indicatorNotes.with: 'with' sets the pieces side by side

blocks.note: d = daughter, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A daughter's holiday card reports that the pier has been cut, with a joke about jobs and cars.
annotation.walkthrough: The quoted line looks like the message itself, but it is only fodder; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: the card sent home from a seaside holiday.

entries.clue: Rum Cola - a cup that's found in Mexico (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a place described by where it is

indicatorNotes.Rum: rum as an adjective means odd, so the letters come out strangely

annotation.surface: A cup of rum and cola, the drink of a Mexican beach resort.
annotation.walkthrough: Rum sits beside cola as a drink, but here it means strange.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by location: the Pacific resort city lies in Mexico.

entries.clue: Dope found in clubs - large amount (4)

blocks.note: a lot is a large amount

annotation.surface: A news item: plenty of drugs turned up in nightclubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs to go with 'clubs', but it means an idiot.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are informal British words for a fool.

entries.clue: Officer in charge getting in staff painter (6,9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places IC inside the word for staff

blocks.note: a pole is a staff, a long stick
John Constable, the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain

annotation.surface: An officer in charge brings a painter onto the staff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees but is a stick.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the constable is the basic rank of British police officer.

entries.clue: Boozer is outspoken initially, times ten (5)

indicatorNotes.initially, times ten: only the first letter is multiplied by ten

blocks.note: the first letter V is Roman 5; ten times it is 50, Roman L

annotation.surface: A drinker is loud at first and ten times louder later.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the letters as Roman numerals: V (5) times ten is L (50), which turns VOCAL into the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: your regular pub is your local, and boozer is slang for a pub.

entries.clue: I landed in pet's poo running across the street? (8)

indicatorNotes.landed in: I lands inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.running: running like a liquid, so the letters go out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, rearranged around the I

annotation.surface: Someone treads in a dog's mess as they run across the road.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: the house across the street faces yours.

entries.clue: Central elements of gospel echo and echo, losing nothing in delivery (6)

indicatorNotes.Central elements of: take the letters at the centre of the word
indicatorNotes.losing: drop the O from the second echo

blocks.note: the middle two of the six letters of GOSPEL
the first letter of echo, which is also its letter in the NATO radio alphabet
ECHO without O, the round zero for nothing

annotation.surface: A preacher's delivery of the gospel echoes and echoes around the church.
annotation.walkthrough: The two echoes are used differently: one is the radio letter E, the other is the word itself minus its O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a speaker's delivery is the manner of their talk.

entries.clue: Paper hat for a dunce? (8)

blocks.note: a traditional British size of writing paper, slightly longer than A4
the cone-shaped cap a fool was made to wear, read as a possessive

annotation.surface: A paper hat made for the class dunce.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word: FOOL'S CAP.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a paper size, and the cap a fool or dunce was made to wear.

entries.clue: Warmer at night with a partner? (7)

annotation.definition: Warmer at night with a partner?

blocks.note: the surface pushes a hot-water bottle or a blanket; the setter means something worn on the foot in bed
sounds like a bedfellow, but means the other one of a pair

annotation.surface: Someone says they sleep warmer with a partner beside them.
annotation.walkthrough: The partner sounds like a bedfellow, but it is the other sock of the pair.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a sock warms the foot in bed, and socks always come in pairs.

entries.clue: Catches Conservative coming out for Republican, in ecstasies (8)

indicatorNotes.coming out for: C leaves and R takes its place

annotation.surface: A Conservative defects to the Republicans, and someone is thrilled at the catch.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface borrows 'coming out' from party switching; here it just swaps the C of CAPTURES for R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the plural: states of intense delight.

entries.clue: Notes orders - could be something fishy (6)

blocks.note: musical notes arranged in rising or falling order
fishy read literally: the covering a fish wears

annotation.surface: Someone notes that the orders look suspicious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests something suspicious, but it is literal: it belongs to a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: notes played in order, and the plates on a fish's skin.

entries.clue: Occasionally dropped flipping jelly baby in red ooze (7)

indicatorNotes.Occasionally dropped: every other letter is dropped, leaving only occasional ones
indicatorNotes.flipping: the kept letters are flipped to run backwards

blocks.note: every second letter: jElLy BaBy In ReD
reversal indicator: the kept letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A red jelly baby, dropped on the floor, oozes stickily.
annotation.walkthrough: A jelly baby is a British baby-shaped gummy sweet. 'Dropped' belongs to the indicator, not the scene: every other letter falls away before the flip.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to trickle out slowly.

entries.clue: One holding valuable stock certainly bust after rate fluctuates (8,5)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' puts SURE CHEST later in the order than the rearranged rate
indicatorNotes.fluctuates: the letters of rate move about

blocks.note: the bust is the upper body

annotation.surface: A stockholder is certain to go broke once the interest rate moves.
annotation.walkthrough: Stock and rate point at finance, and 'bust' at bankruptcy; bust here is anatomy.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a box of gold and jewels holds valuable stock.

entries.clue: Calculated coming from Budapest - I'm at Edinburgh (9)

indicatorNotes.coming from: the answer comes out of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A traveller works out a route from Budapest to Edinburgh.
annotation.walkthrough: The two capitals look like a journey but only supply letters across the word breaks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: worked out roughly by reckoning.

entries.clue: Chemical compound sustaining a heavenly body (8)

indicatorNotes.sustaining: in a down clue, the compound holds up A from below

blocks.note: a class of organic compound, like cholesterol or testosterone

annotation.surface: A chemical compound keeps a heavenly body going.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sustaining' is positional: the compound sits below A in the grid, supporting it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the minor planets orbiting the sun are heavenly bodies.

entries.clue: Follow case in which collaborators oppose the government (6,7)

annotation.definition: in which collaborators oppose the government

blocks.note: a cabinet is a display case

annotation.surface: A legal case in which collaborators turn against the government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' sounds legal but is a piece of furniture.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the British opposition's front bench, colleagues who face the government's ministers.

entries.clue: Likely Lads singularly funny at first (4-2)

indicatorNotes.at first: 'at first' puts ODD at the front, as something done at first comes before the rest

annotation.surface: Praise for the sitcom The Likely Lads, each funny in his own way.
annotation.walkthrough: The Likely Lads was a British sitcom, so the capital L makes 'Likely' look part of a title. 'Singularly' asks for one lad.
annotation.definitionFit: A betting idiom: a favourite quoted at short odds is likely to win.

entries.clue: Enormity when extracting or creating bad blood (6)

indicatorNotes.when extracting: OR is pulled out of the word

annotation.surface: A grave wrong that stirs up bad blood.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits close to 'enormity' in sense, which hides that the word itself is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hostility between people is bad blood.

entries.clue: Total over one hundred and 13? (5)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, SUM is turned over to read upward

annotation.surface: A sum: add a hundred and thirteen to the total.
annotation.walkthrough: 13 is not a number but a pointer to 13 across, SCALES; the question mark says scales are one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: scales, the answer to 13, are a part of music.

entries.clue: Inconvenient being unwell before I'm visiting Ted (3-5)

indicatorNotes.before: 'before' means earlier in order, so ILL comes ahead of the rest
indicatorNotes.visiting: I'M visits TED, going inside him

annotation.surface: Someone apologises for visiting Ted while they are ill, at a bad time.
annotation.walkthrough: Ted is just a name supplying letters, and 'visiting' puts I'M inside him.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: coming at a bad moment.

entries.clue: Plot to get pot, student's admitted (4)

indicatorNotes.admitted: to be admitted is to be let in, so L is let inside PAN

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking pot

annotation.surface: A student confesses to a scheme to get hold of cannabis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pot' suggests cannabis beside 'student', but it is a cooking pan. The L comes from British learner-driver plates.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scheme, as in a plot to do something.

entries.clue: Escaping from kennel, cat's boldly overturned barrier (8)

indicatorNotes.Escaping from: the answer gets out of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.overturned: the letters are turned over to run backwards

blocks.note: reversal indicator: the hidden letters are turned upside down

annotation.surface: A cat breaks out of a kennel and knocks over the barrier on its way.
annotation.walkthrough: The escape story makes 'barrier' feel like part of the scene, but it is the definition, standing apart at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something standing in the way.

entries.clue: Sinks Swedish group half-heartedly installed backwards (6)

indicatorNotes.half-heartedly: one of the two letters at the heart is lost
indicatorNotes.backwards: 'backwards' means in reverse direction, so SET is read from its last letter

blocks.note: ABBA, the Swedish pop group, loses one of its two central Bs

annotation.surface: Someone sinks an ABBA album into the player the wrong way round.
annotation.walkthrough: ABBA were the Swedish pop group who won Eurovision in 1974. 'Half-heartedly' removes only half of the heart, one B.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the intransitive verb: a storm dies down.

entries.clue: Books written by, say, Fifties degenerate (8)

indicatorNotes.written by: NT is written next to the other piece

blocks.note: the Fifties are an example of a ten-year span
NT = New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: A critic dismisses books by writers of the Fifties as degenerate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' looks like novels but is the New Testament; 'say' signals that the Fifties are one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe moral decline.

entries.clue: Cloudy ale drunk, end in a bad way (6)

indicatorNotes.in a bad way: the letters of end are in a mess

annotation.surface: Cloudy ale is drunk and the drinker ends up in a bad way.
annotation.walkthrough: Two separate small anagrams sit side by side; 'cloudy' goes with the beer in the surface, but it describes the sky.
annotation.definitionFit: A weather sense: a heavy grey sky, the colour of lead.
